title: HON’BLE PRESIDENT OF INDIA SMT DROUPADI MURMU REVIEWS PASSING OUT PARADE OF AUTUMN TERM 2026 AT INDIAN NAVAL ACADEMY, EZHIMALA
body_text: The Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala conducted the Passing Out Parade (POP) of Autumn Term 2026 on 28 Nov 2026, marking the culmination of rigorous ab-initio military training of 427 trainees, including 69 women trainees. The ceremonial parade marked a defining transition in the lives of the passing-out trainees as they marched to the ‘Antim Pag’ – the final step – at the magnificent Pereira Parade Ground. That single step marks the beginning of their commissioned service in the Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard and maritime forces of friendly foreign countries. The passing out cohort included 18 trainees from Nine Friendly Foreign Countries – Bangladesh, Kenya, Malawi, Maldives Myanmar, Oman, Seychelles, Tanzania and Timor Leste – further strengthening the Academy’s role in fostering enduring bonds of friendship and professional camaraderie among maritime forces. The Parade was reviewed by the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, as the Chief Guest. Presence of the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces added a special significance to this ceremonial occasion. The parade was also witnessed by Shri Om Prakash Mathur, Hon’ble Governor of Keralam, Shri Roji M. John, Minister of Higher Education in the Government of Kerala, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, the Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Sameer Saxena, the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command, senior officers of the Indian Navy, distinguished guests, foreign Military Attachés, instructors, training staff as well as proud parents and families of the passing-out trainees. During the Parade, the Hon’ble President conferred medals and trophies to trainees who distinguished themselves during training. The President’s Gold Medal for standing first in the 111th Indian Naval Academy Course was awarded to Midshipman Kaushik Singh. The FOC-in-C (South) Trophy for Best Foreign Cadet was conferred upon Midshipman MD Fidel Reza from Bangladesh. Midshipman Shivani Singh received the FOC in C (South) Trophy for being first in Overall order of merit among passing out ex NDA trainees. The CNS Gold Medals for Best Trainees in the 42nd Naval Orientation Course (Extended) and 43rd Naval Orientation Course (Regular) were awarded to Cadet Somesh Sharma and Cadet Asia Verma respectively. The Director General Coast Guard Trophy for Best Coast Guard Trainee was awarded to Cadet Mitesh Dinesh Rane of the 42nd Naval Orientation (Coast Guard) Course. Addressing the passing-out trainees, the Hon’ble President congratulated them on successfully completing their training and embarking upon a life dedicated to service to the nation. The Hon’ble President also acknowledged the contributions of instructors and training staff in shaping the young officers during their formative years at INA. A defining moment of the ceremony was the time-honoured ‘Shipping of Stripes’, symbolising the conferment of commissioned officer rank upon the passing-out trainees. The Chief of the Naval Staff joined the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command, the Commandant, INA, other senior Naval officers and proud parents to ship the stripes of Sub Lieutenant rank on the broad shoulders of newly commissioned officers.
